concept.title: Creating a Strong Password
concept.shortdesc: A strong Wi-Fi password helps prevent unauthorized access to the wireless network and connected devices.

section.title: Purpose of a Wi-Fi Password
section.p: The controls access to the wireless network identified by .
A user or device must provide the correct password before the permits access to the wireless network.
section.note: The Wi-Fi password is case-sensitive. Uppercase and lowercase letters are different characters.

section.title: Strong Password Requirements
section.p: Create a password that is difficult to guess but easy for an authorized user to enter correctly.
A strong Wi-Fi password has the following characteristics:

ul.li: It is long.
It is unique to the Wi-Fi network.
It does not contain personal information.
It does not contain a common word or predictable pattern.
It contains a combination of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and permitted special characters.

section.note: Use the password length and character requirements specified by the .
Password length is more important than unnecessary complexity. Use a long passphrase if the supports spaces and the required client devices can enter the passphrase correctly.

section.title: Information to Avoid
section.p: Do not include the following information in the password:

ul.li: Your name or the name of another person
Your address, telephone number, or date of birth
The product name or model number
The Wi-Fi network name
Repeated or sequential characters
A password that you use for another account

section.note: Do not use the default Wi-Fi password after the initial setup.

section.title: Separate Wi-Fi and Administrator Passwords
section.p: Use different passwords for the wireless network and the .
The permits devices to connect to the Wi-Fi network. The administrator password permits an authorized user to change settings in the .
section.note: If an unauthorized user obtains the Wi-Fi password, the separate administrator password helps protect the router configuration.

section.title: Password Examples
section.p: The following examples show weak password patterns. Do not use these patterns:

ul.li: A short password, such asPassword1
A number sequence, such as 12345678
A password that contains the SSID
A repeated character pattern, such as aaaaaaaa

section.p: A stronger password can use a long combination of unrelated words, numbers, and permitted special characters.
section.note: The examples in this topic are for explanation only. Do not use an example password on an operational network.

section.title: Password Storage and Sharing
section.p: Store the Wi-Fi password in a secure location. Use a trusted password manager when one is available.
Share the primary Wi-Fi password only with authorized users. Use for visitors and devices that do not require access to the primary network.
section.note: Do not store the Wi-Fi password in an unprotected document, email message, or shared file. Limit access to stored network credentials.

section.title: When to Change the Password
section.p: Change the Wi-Fi password in the following situations:

ul.li: The current password is a default password.
An unauthorized person knows the password.
An unknown device connects to the network.
The password appears in an unprotected location.
A security policy requires a password change.

section.p: After you change the password, reconnect each authorized device by using the new .
section.note: A password change disconnects devices that use the previous password. Update all authorized devices after the change.
